title: Universal Black-Box nAE-to-nvAE Transformation
summary: Hash-based key derivation is readily proved secure only in the random-oracle model; a universal black-box nAE-to-nvAE transformation in the standard model remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether there exists a black-box transformation $\Gamma$ that converts every nAE-secure authenticated-encryption scheme $\Pi$ into an nvAE-secure variable-stretch scheme $\Gamma(\Pi)$, with security established in the standard model. A suggested hash-based key-derivation transformation is easily proved secure only in the random-oracle model and adds unnecessary complexity, while other described transformations apply only to large subsets of nAE-secure schemes rather than to every such scheme.

scope.domain: Variable-stretch nonce-based authenticated encryption and universal black-box transformations.
assumptions: The input authenticated-encryption scheme is nAE-secure.
Security must be established in the standard model.
parameters: Π: an arbitrary nAE-secure authenticated-encryption scheme
Γ: the sought black-box transformation whose output Γ(Π) must be nvAE-secure
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a standard-model black-box transformation exists that works for every nAE-secure authenticated-encryption scheme.

progress.summary: The paper gives a hash-based approach that is easily proved secure only in the random-oracle model and describes transformations covering large subsets of nAE schemes. It explicitly leaves the universal standard-model treatment open.
citation_labels: Reza Reyhanitabar et al., Authenticated Encryption with Variable Stretch
